title: Camunda IDP and the ABBYY partnership do not close the business-record gap
content:
Camunda IDP is documented as using *"artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to identify, extract, and organize data from your structured and unstructured documents"*. The ABBYY partnership of 19 December 2025 delivers an ABBYY Vantage connector for *"classification, extraction, validation, and human-in-the-loop capabilities"*.

Both are real, both shipped in the stated window, and neither has any bearing on whether Camunda keeps an immutable attributed log of business decisions. "Document" in Intelligent Document Processing means a scanned invoice; "document" in a document-model platform means a typed state machine. The two senses share a word and nothing else.

The practical warning is about screening method: a vendor announcement can occupy the same vocabulary as your thesis without occupying the same slot. Anyone who ruled Camunda out on this basis ruled it out for the wrong reason — and would have missed that the gap actually did close, elsewhere, in release 8.9.
description: Both are optical and LLM extraction from scanned documents; treating them as an audit capability conflates document processing with a typed record of decisions.
